g.data-tip:
**Process** · microcamd — our daemon, owns the whole chain
Ours: builds and tears down the blocks in an order the SoC does not hang on, and picks the cheapest transition between states [R]

**Vendor library** · 3A (libcus3a, libispalgo) — exposure and white balance
Limits: exposure 300–14000 µs, gain ×1–×8 at start [R]
Ours: inside microcamd: every frame, from the ISP statistics, sets the sensor's exposure and gain, and the ISP's balance [R]

**Process** · microcam-menu — our menu program, the scene's owner
Ours: gets the remote's keys and the camera's state from microcamd over the control socket, sends it the whole scene and the settings; started by `app-start.sh` after microcamd and restarted when it dies or hangs [R]

**Device** · the IR remote and the SoC's IR decoder (rc-core, `mstar ir`)
Limits: one key at a time — a second key while one is held gives nothing; the kernel repeats a held key from ~505 ms every 140 ms [R]
Ours: microcamd's keys thread reads it [R]

**SoC block** · GE — 2D engine, blitter
Limits: copies, blends, stretches rectangles; synchronous, no channels or ports [R]
Ours: builds the menu windows from tiles for the ui thread [R]

**Kernel module** · microcam_rgn — our windows over the frame
Limits: up to 8 windows per port; handles 0–1023; GOP shows 8 per frame [R]
Ours: ARGB4444 canvases in the media heap, 2–3 per window, for HDMI, USB, recording and photo [R]

**Kernel module** · microcam_canvas — the frames the encoders read
Limits: up to 4 pools of 8 canvases, up to 4 readers per pool; a port's window from a column that is a multiple of 16 [R]
Ours: a pool of canvases per output (HDMI pool 2, USB 0, recording and photo 1); gives a port a window in a free canvas and each reader (an encoder, DISP) the whole canvas, and sees by itself when the reader let it go; JPEG 3, H.264 4, DISP 5 [R]. Stamps the time a canvas is lent to the port and let go by each reader (`/proc/microcam_canvas_lent`, `/proc/microcam_canvas_holds`): from them microcamd keeps the sensor in step with the monitor and hands DISP a canvas the moment it is lent to the port, while the port still writes it [R]

**External device** · GC8613 sensor — the camera's image sensor
Limits: RAW10, 4K up to 45 fps, 1080p up to 121, MIPI CSI-2 [R]
Ours: the only source of the picture

**SoC block** · MIPI-CSI + VIF — sensor capture
Limits: 4 CSI-2 receivers, 4 groups, 16 devices, 8 hardware pipes; realtime only on pipes 0–2 and port 0 [R]
Ours: pad 0 → dev 0 → port 0 → ISP as lines [R]

**SoC block** · ISP — raw to colour
Limits: one device, up to 32 channels (the kernel module allows 16) [R]
Ours: dev 0, channel 0 [R]

**SoC block** · SCL — scalers
Limits: 6 hardware scalers HWSCL0–5, each one output of one device; output width HWSCL0/1 up to 4608, HWSCL2–5 up to 3840; up to 34 channels, 6 ports per channel [R][S]
Ours: dev 0, 1 and 3 [R]

**SoC block** · GOP over the SCL outputs — overlays
Limits: 8 windows per GOP; I8/I4/I2/ARGB1555/ARGB4444, no stretching [R]
Ours: the menu over the live window on HDMI, USB, in the recording, photo and zoom — GOP 0–3 [R]

**SoC block** · DISP — display
Limits: two devices; ports only enlarge (up to 16×), NV12 only; layer 0's windows do not overlap; HDMI, VGA, CVBS, TTL, MIPI-DSI, BT601/656/1120 [R][S]
Ours: DISP0 on HDMI [R]

**SoC block** · HDMI-TX — HDMI transmitter
Limits: HDMI 1.4, up to 4K30 / 1080p60; no ports of its own, follows DISP's scan-out [R][S]
Ours: the best mode by the monitor's EDID [R]
**External device** · monitor over HDMI

**SoC block** · VENC — encoders
Limits: channels 0–32, up to 17 at once; H.26x up to 4096×2176, JPEG up to 8192×8192; H.264 4K ≈ 29.5 fps [R][S]
Ours: dev 0 and dev 8, two channels each [R]

**Kernel modules** · g_webcam + UDC — a USB camera, network and disk for the PC
Limits: USB 2.0; the controller has separate in and out FIFOs only on ep5 [R]
Ours: our modules — UVC (ep1, ep3), RNDIS (ep5 in+out, ep6), mass storage with the SD card (ep4, ep2) [R]
**External device** · PC over USB

**External device** · SD card
Ours: recording and photo; on command, the host's disk over USB [R]

**Pool** · media heap (MMA) — the DRAM shared by frames and hardware buffers
Limits: 176 MB, set in U-Boot (`mma_heap`) [R]
Ours: the strip is `microcam mem` of 2026-11-14: 110.6 used, 65.4 free [R]. USB in H.264/H.265 instead of MJPEG takes the SCL→encoder ring 11.9 and the H.264 encoder 19.8 instead of the JPEG ring (measured 2026-11-11) [R]
g.text: media heap (MMA) · 176 MB · measured 2026-11-14: HDMI 2160p30 + USB MJPEG 4K45 in the shared frame, the menu up

g.data-tip:
**Pool** · Linux RAM — the memory of the processes and the kernel
Limits: 74.3 MB (MemTotal) [R]
Ours: 20.8 MB available in the same measurement, microcamd resident 26.1; the tile layers' budget `LAYER_BYTES` 12 MiB [R]

**microcamd thread** · control — takes the scene, commands and settings
Ours: Unix socket `/tmp/microcam.sock` (pictures through memfd) and TCP 7700 [R]; the camera's settings as one list whoever changes them — the menu, the USB host, the CLI — every picture knob sent to the ISP after each IQ load; the ones the user set saved to `/customer/microcam/settings.json` [R]

**microcamd thread** · keys — the remote
Ours: reads `/dev/input/event0` and sends each key, its press, repeats and release, to the scene's owner alone; `key` from any connection writes a press into the same device, so it comes back as the remote's with the kernel's repeats [R]

**microcamd thread** · pipeline — builds the hardware
Ours: sets up and tears down VIF, ISP, SCL, DISP, VENC; SCL dev 3 copies for pictures; every 5 s trims the sensor's frame length (vts) so a frame arrives ~5 ms before DISP's pass [R]

**microcamd thread** · res — pictures
Ours: JPEG from the card through JPD and SCL dev 3 into NV12 / ABGR in the media heap (the CPU only for what JPD does not take); reads the file's header, makes the small form from its thumbnail; an MP4's picture is its cover [R]

**microcamd thread** · feed — hands out the frames
Ours: takes the frames of the SCL ports (the pools' canvases) and hands them to the pool's readers — the encoders and DISP — with no copy; frames beyond a reader's rate it returns evenly [R]. With a live picture and no overlays it hands DISP the canvas the moment it is lent to the port — DISP scans ~3.5 ms behind the writing [R]

**microcamd thread** · ui — draws the menu
Limits: menu budget 24 MiB for tiles and pictures [R]
Ours: tiny-skia tiles in the media heap; GE builds each output's windows from them [R]

**microcamd thread** · uvc-pump — sending to USB
Ours: takes a compressed frame as soon as it is ready and puts it into a free gadget buffer; the host always gets the newest [R]

**microcamd thread** · recorder — recording
Ours: writes MP4 and JPEG photos to the card; into each MP4 of ours a cover, a 480×270 still of its first frame [R]

**microcamd thread** · card — owner of the SD card
Ours: mounts and lets go of the card on kernel events (the vendor's mdev hook is off), hands it to the host as a removable disk and takes it back [R]

**microcamd thread** · player — the player
Ours: reads the MP4 samples from the card one by one and hands them to VDEC at the file's times; on pause asks VDEC to decode the current sample again at the file's rate [R]

**CSI-2 receivers** · pads 0–3 — one per sensor
Ours: pad 0 [R]

**VIF device** · dev 0 — group 0, MIPI
Limits: MIPI linear only on dev 0, 4, 8, 12 [R]
Ours: takes the sensor [R]

**VIF devices** · dev 1–15
Limits: by the SDK 8 of the 16 are usable — which ones is unknown [S]
Ours: unused

**ISP channel** · 0 — the sensor's stream
Ours: the only one [R]

**ISP port** · 0 — the live output
Limits: realtime only, and only into SCL dev 0 [R]
Ours: into SCL dev 0 [R]

**ISP port** · 1 — YUV DMA into memory
Limits: YUYV / NV12 / 422SP [R]
Ours: unused

**ISP port** · 2 — the IR plane
Limits: for RGB-IR sensors; only together with port 0 or 1 [R]
Ours: unused

**ISP channels** · 1–31
Ours: unused

**SCL device** · dev 0, channel 0 — the main scaler
Limits: input only from the ISP, realtime; port p = the mask's p-th scaler [R]
Ours: mask 7 → HWSCL0, 1, 2 [R]

**SCL device** · dev 1 — zoom
Limits: input from memory or from JPD, realtime [R]
Ours: mask 8 → HWSCL3; three channels share it in time, working only during a zoom [R]

**SCL device** · dev 2 — scaling straight from VIF
Limits: only from VIF, realtime; a bind from memory is refused [R]
Ours: unused

**SCL device** · dev 3 — StretchBuf, memory to memory
Limits: rotation 90/180/270 only here; mask 0x20 → HWSCL5 is required [R]
Ours: scales the pictures to their windows (once) and turns NV12 ↔ ARGB bands when baking the menu [R]

**Scaler** · HWSCL4 — free
Limits: by default its output is GOP 4's overlay [R]
Ours: unused (dev 1 in probes) [R]

**GOP** · 0 — over HWSCL0, the HDMI port
Ours: the HDMI menu over the live window [R]

**GOP** · 1 — over HWSCL1
Ours: the menu in the recording and photo [R]

**GOP** · 2 — over HWSCL2
Ours: the menu on USB [R]

**GOP** · 3 — over HWSCL3
Ours: the menu over the zoom frames, both channels [R]

**GOP** · 4 — over HWSCL4
Ours: unused

**GOP** · 5 — over DIVP
Limits: other masks give it to LDC or HWSCL5 [R]
Ours: unused

**DISP device** · DISP0
Ours: drives HDMI [R]

**DISP device** · DISP1 — the second display
Limits: layers 2 and 3, GOP 8/9; whether it can drive HDMI on our board is not checked [R]
Ours: unused

**DISP block** · WBC — screen capture into memory
Limits: one DMA, NV12, downscale only [R]
Ours: only in our probes [R]

**VENC device** · dev 0 — H.264 / H.265, one Wave5 core
Ours: USB and recording [R]

**VENC device** · dev 8 — JPEG (JPE)
Ours: USB MJPEG and photo [R]

**SoC block** · JPD — JPEG decoder
Limits: dev 0, channels 0–15, one YUYV output: into SCL dev 1 realtime or into memory; the input is padded with zeros to 16 bytes, otherwise some files never finish [R]
Ours: the menu's pictures — channel 0 for the time of a decode, the file from the media heap, YUYV into memory scaled down ½–⅛, then SCL dev 3; thumbnails of our photos [R]

**SoC block** · VDEC — video decoder (Wave5, shared with the H.26x encoder)
Limits: dev 0, 32 channels; port 0 scales down to 1/8; 4K ~31 ms per frame, beside H.264 4K30 USB both are slower [R]
Ours: the player — channel 0, port 0 bound into the outputs' SCL dev 1 channels while a file is shown; the device is held until microcamd exits [R]

**SoC block** · LDC — lens distortion correction
Limits: dev 0, channels 0–15, one input and one output [R]
Ours: unused

**SoC block** · DIVP — video processing on the SCL banks
Limits: no mi_divp of its own on the camera; the number of channels is unknown [R]
Ours: unused

**SoC block** · IPU — neural accelerator
Limits: up to 48 channels, a network per channel; off the picture's path [R]
Ours: unused

**Buffer** · the canvases of pool 2 (microcam_canvas) — HDMI frames, read too by the USB encoder and the recording encoder when their frame equals the HDMI frame
Limits: canvases of 12.0 MB (4K NV12, 2176 lines), counted from what each reader holds and its rate — 5 with DISP alone at 30 or beside a 4K25 recording, 6 beside USB MJPEG 4K45; one more with a picture pasted in [R]
Ours: SCL port 0 writes the live picture into them, pictures and the menu lie there beforehand; DISP and JPEG read them whole by reference [R]

**Buffer** · the menu's canvases (microcam_rgn) — the menu windows GOP lays over the SCL outputs
Limits: 10 canvases, 19.8 MB in this measurement [R]
Ours: the menu program's scene, drawn by GE [R]

**Buffer** · microcamd's own media memory — the GE and baking bands, staging
Limits: microcamd's share is what the video leaves (84.7 MB in this measurement) [R]
Ours: 6.4 MB [R]
**Buffer** · the H.26x device (Wave5): mma_heap_codec 4.0 + vcodec_dev 0.9 — held from the first H.26x channel on [R]

**Buffer** · the output ring of the USB JPEG encoder — compressed frames
Limits: 3.1 MB at 4K45 in this measurement [R]
Ours: uvc-pump takes the frames from it [R]
**Buffer** · CMDQ — the engines' command queues, 3.0 MB [R]
**Buffer** · interbuf 2.0, ISP, logs, GE 0.6 — 2.6 MB [R]
**Free** · 65.4 MB in this measurement [R]
**Used** · about 53.5 MB: processes and kernel (74.3 − 20.8 available), microcamd 26.1 of it
**Available** · 20.8 MB (MemAvailable) in this measurement [R]

**CSI pad** · 0 — MIPI receiver
Ours: our sensor [R]

**CSI pad** · 1 — MIPI receiver
Ours: unused

**CSI pad** · 2 — MIPI receiver
Ours: unused

**CSI pad** · 3 — MIPI receiver
Ours: unused

**VIF port** · dev 0, port 0 — the whole frame, unscaled
Limits: the only one that runs realtime [R]
Ours: lines into the ISP [R]

**VIF port** · dev 0, port 1 — crop into memory
Ours: unused

**SCL port** · dev 0, port 0 — HWSCL0's output
Limits: width up to 4608 [S]
Ours: HDMI's live window, writes straight into the canvases of pool 2 [R]

**SCL port** · dev 0, port 1 — HWSCL1's output
Limits: width up to 4608 [S]
Ours: the recording and photo frame, writes straight into the canvases of pool 1; off while the recording frame equals the HDMI or the USB frame [R]

**SCL port** · dev 0, port 2 — HWSCL2's output
Limits: width up to 3840 [S]
Ours: the USB frame, writes straight into the canvases of pool 0; off while the USB frame equals the HDMI frame [R]; in H.264/H.265 with one live picture and no zoom it writes a ring tied to the encoder [R]

**SCL port** · dev 0, port 3
Limits: not available with mask 7 (INVALID_PORTID) [R]
Ours: unused

**SCL port** · dev 0, port 4
Limits: not available with mask 7 [R]
Ours: unused

**SCL port** · dev 0, port 5
Limits: not available with mask 7 [R]
Ours: unused

**SCL channel** · dev 1, channel 0 — port 0 on HWSCL3
Ours: enlarges port 2's crop for USB [R]

**SCL channel** · dev 1, channel 1 — port 0 on HWSCL3
Ours: enlarges port 1's crop for the recording [R]

**SCL channel** · dev 1, channel 2 — port 0 on HWSCL3
Ours: enlarges port 0's crop for HDMI during a zoom (DISP no longer scales: the menu lies in the canvas); while a file is shown it writes VDEC's frame into the HDMI pool [R]

**SCL channel** · dev 3, 0x20 — the driver's internal channel
Ours: through StretchBuf [R]

**SCL channel** · dev 3, 0x21 — the driver's internal channel

g.data-tip: HDMI frame. The port writes the live picture **straight into a canvas** of microcam_canvas (pool 2); DISP reads the whole canvas **by reference**, 1:1; no copy of the live picture. Pictures, black and the menu over them lie in the canvas beforehand (GE). canvases counted from what each reader holds and its rate: 5 for DISP alone at 30, 6 beside USB MJPEG 4K45 (one more with a picture pasted in); a closed frame: the port is off, 3 canvases, a canvas is handed on by the feed clock. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; paint-order: stroke; stroke: rgb(15, 18, 22); stroke-width: 4px; stroke-linejoin: round;

g.data-tip: USB frame. The port writes the live picture **straight into a canvas** of microcam_canvas (a window in the canvas or the whole canvas); the encoder takes the whole canvas **by reference**; no copy of the live picture. Pictures, black and the menu over them lie in the canvas beforehand (GE). canvases counted as for HDMI: 3 at 4K45 (one more with a picture pasted in); a closed frame: the port is off, a canvas is handed on by the feed clock. When the USB frame equals the HDMI frame, this port and pool are not built: the encoder reads the HDMI pool. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; paint-order: stroke; stroke: rgb(15, 18, 22); stroke-width: 4px; stroke-linejoin: round;

g.data-tip: USB in the shared frame: when the USB frame equals the HDMI frame (size, menu level, crop, layout), the USB encoder is a **second reader** of the HDMI pool, by reference, at its own rate (it takes a canvas when the canvas's capture time reaches its next one); USB then has no port, pool, menu layer or bake of its own. The reader is added and removed with no HDMI step. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; paint-order: stroke; stroke: rgb(15, 18, 22); stroke-width: 4px; stroke-linejoin: round;

g.data-tip: USB frame in H.264/H.265 when it holds only the live picture with no zoom: the port is **tied to the encoder by a ring** (HW_RING, a one-frame ring, 11.9 MB at 4K); the encoder reads the bands right behind the writing — the stream ~1 ms after the last line. Otherwise canvases, as for MJPEG. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; display: none;

g.data-tip: Recording frame when it is its own (equal to neither the HDMI nor the USB frame). The port writes **straight into a canvas** of microcam_canvas; the H.264 encoder takes the whole canvas by reference; no copy; canvases counted as for HDMI: 4 at 4K25. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; paint-order: stroke; stroke: rgb(15, 18, 22); stroke-width: 4px; stroke-linejoin: round;

g.data-tip: Photo: the port's frame, composed for the shot together with the menu (GOP); feed hands it to the JPEG encoder; no copy, one frame. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; display: none;

g.data-tip: Recording in the shared frame: when the recording frame equals the HDMI frame (size, what is shown, crop, layout), the H.264 encoder is one more reader of the HDMI pool, by reference, at its own rate; port 1, the recording pool and its menu layer are not built. At 4K beside DISP and USB JPEG: holds a canvas 29 ms, all canvases, 25 fps [R 2026-11-10]. Otherwise the USB frame, otherwise its own.

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; display: none;

g.data-tip: Photo during a recording: JPEG channel 2 is a reader of the pool the recording reads, handed one finished canvas; no copy. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; display: none;

g.data-tip: Zoom: the port's crop by an **MI_SYS bind** through memory (FRAME_BASE) → the zoom scaler; MI_SYS moves it. From there feed hands its frame to the encoder. [R]

g.data-tip: Mounts the card on /mnt when it is inserted, lets it go when it is removed (kernel events); with the card removed it stops the recording and the player. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; paint-order: stroke; stroke: rgb(15, 18, 22); stroke-width: 4px; stroke-linejoin: round;

g.data-tip: The whole card (/dev/mmcblk0) as the host's removable disk (a mass-storage LUN), on the command `card share`; meanwhile it is not mounted on the camera, photo and recording are refused. Back: `card take` or ejecting it on the host. [R]

g.data-tip: While a file is shown: VDEC port 0 by an **MI_SYS bind** (FRAME_BASE) into the output's channel on SCL dev 1 — HDMI and, if USB has its own frame, channel 0; the output's SCL port 0 is silent. The menu: RGN on the channel's port. [R]

g.data-tip: Decoded NV12 picture in the media heap (the menu's budget); one for all outputs, held while the scene shows it. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; paint-order: stroke; stroke: rgb(15, 18, 22); stroke-width: 4px; stroke-linejoin: round;

g.data-tip: GE puts into the outputs' canvases (HDMI, USB, recording) the pictures (scaled once by SCL dev 3), black and the menu over the pictures; on a change of layout or menu; with a picture over the live one, every frame. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; paint-order: stroke; stroke: rgb(15, 18, 22); stroke-width: 4px; stroke-linejoin: round;

g.data-tip: ui calls GE: tiles → each output's windows; at every change of the menu. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; paint-order: stroke; stroke: rgb(15, 18, 22); stroke-width: 4px; stroke-linejoin: round;

g.data-tip: Baking the menu over the pictures of each still frame, HDMI too, once for the outputs showing the same: SCL dev 3 turns a band of the NV12 picture into ARGB8888 and back into an NV12 patch, GE between them lays the menu as in an RGN layer (4 bits); called from the ui thread, synchronous, at every change of the menu over pictures. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; paint-order: stroke; stroke: rgb(15, 18, 22); stroke-width: 4px; stroke-linejoin: round;

g.data-tip: GE writes the menu windows into microcam_rgn canvases (ARGB4444), 2–3 per window; on a change. [R]

text.style: text-anchor: middle; font-size: 15px; paint-order: stroke; stroke: rgb(15, 18, 22); stroke-width: 4px; stroke-linejoin: round;

g.data-tip: GOP 0 reads the canvases of the HDMI menu windows by DMA, every frame. [R]
